Western volunteers, including Americans, are joining Kurdish and other militia groups to fight ISIS in Iraq and Syria, motivated by a mix of idealized and online recruitment drives. While the Kurdish Peshmerga forces oppose the use of foreign fighters, U.S. military personnel and law enforcement continue training local troops, as some volunteers describe the fight as a necessary defense against ISIS' expansion.

V Diesel humorously predicted "Furious 7" will win an Oscar, but the joke lands on the franchise's consistent diverse cast and strong box office performance. The "Fast" films have featured multiracial leads—Hispanic, black, Samoan, and Beninese—who have proven profitable at the box office, with Hispanics account for 25% of frequent moviegoers despite make up 17% of the U.S. population.

California's Department of Public Health has declared the measles outbreak over after 42 days with no new cases. The 131 cases were linked to the B3 strain, with 70% of the 81 unvaccinated patients falling ill. The outbreak was contained through contact tracing, vaccination, and provider education, and originated from Disney park visitors in December.

Thousands of South Africans protested against xenophobia and violence in Durban, spurred by online campaigns like #PeaceMarch. The march was sparked by recent attacks killing five, including immigrants and South Africans, which led to accusations of hate speech by Tim Flack against King Goodwill Zwelithini. Human Rights Commission is now investigating the allegations, while activists like Imtiaz Sooliman argue that the majority of South Africans support foreign nationals despite rising resentment.

A New York cardiologist, Dr. Anthony Moschetto, was charged with solicitation and conspiracy in a scheme to hurt or kill a rival doctor on Long Island. Two of his alleged co-consecutors, James Chmela and James Kalamaras, also pleaded not guilty to arson and burglary charges. Prosecutors allege the plot was motivated by a professional dispute, with Moschetto reportedly offering hit-hire to have the doctor " beaten" or "killed" for thousands of cash.

The U.N. Security Council voted to impose an arms embargo on the Houthi rebels and Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh's supporters, raising the cost for the group that controls Yemen's capital. Russia abstained from the vote, citing the inclusion of sanctions as a problem. In recent weeks, Saudi Arabia has led a coalition that is conducting airstrikes on targets associated with Saleh's supporters and the Houthis, who have emerged as Yemen's most dominant force in recent months. Superman: Dawn of Justice," which was quickly taken down; the footage shows Batman and Superman clashing face-to-face, and the film stars Henry Cavill and Ben Affleck and is set to premiere in Imax theaters on Monday. On Wednesday morning, Snyder teased the trailer by releasing a short excerpt on Twitter. "Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice" will be released on March 25, 2016 and stars Affleck as Batman and Henry Cavill as Superman.

The jury convicted Aaron Hernandez of first-degree murder after a months-long trial, sentencing him to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Deluding over 35 hours across seven days, the panel of 12 jurors found Hernandez guilty despite emotional deliberation and extensive note-taking. The jurors, who largely had little prior knowledge of the case, emphasized they reached their conclusion based solely on the evidence presented in court.

Three men have been arrested in connection with an alleged gang rape that was videotaped during a crowded stretch of Panama City Beach. The third suspect, George Davon Kennedy, was apprehaced in Georgia after investigators linked him to the crime through video evidence. The two other accused, Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee, face sexual battery charges and remain suspended at Troy University, while the victim plans to cooperate with authorities as the investigation continues.

Up to 400 unaccounted service members from the USS Oklahoma will be exhumed this year to be identified. The Defense Department aims to recover and return remains to families with dignity, following the 1941 Pearl Harbor attack that killed 429 sailors and Marines. Historical efforts, including a 93-year-old survivor's testimony, continue to ensure proper identification for next of kin.

Thousands of Syrian and Palestinian refugees trapped in Yarmouk have endured "the deepest circle of hell," with infants Jihad and Mohammad serving as poignant examples of the camp's human toll. The journalist's mission to Damascus underscores that humanitarian action is imperative, arguing that turning away is not an option as the international community must act in a concerted manner to respond to the many tragedies in Syria.

South African authorities detained a 15-year-old girl at Cape Town International Airport after receiving intelligence that she was attempting to leave the country to join ISIS. State Security Minister David Mahlobo stated the minor was radicalized online and planned to join a terrorist group, and she has since released into her family's care while investigations continue. This incident highlights the growing global concern of recruiting young people for terrorist acts, with officials emphasizing continued efforts to clamp such materializing at exit points.

A 20-year-old murder suspect, Kenneth Stancil III, swore and flipped a table during a court hearing regarding the first-degree murder charge of killing a college employee. Authorities arrested him after he was found sleeping on a Florida beach, and he claimed the victim, Ron Lane, deserved to die because he accused him of being a child molaster who made advances to his brother. Reserve Deputy Robert Bates is charged with manslaughter after he shot and killed unarmed suspect Eric Harris, whom he allegedly mistook for his firearm as a Taser during a tussle captured on a police body camera. The Oklahoma NAACP and state and federal investigations are ongoing, as allegations surface that supervisors were told to forge Bates' training records, with the sheriff's office official denying any records had ever been forged. In Garissa, Kenya, a deadly attack at a madrassa was claimed by Al-Shabaab militants, who killed 147 students and injured many others. The suspect, Mohamed Mohamud, a former teacher at the school, is believed to have masterminded the attack from afar near the border with Somalia. Authorities are investigating the recruitment of youth by the group, while the school's Sheikh insists the attacker had no direct link to the school's teachings.

Pope Francis commemorated the Armenian genocide by quoting Pope John Paul II’s 1001 document, which explicitly used the term "genocide," thereby honoring continuity over diplomatic deference. The Pope’s carefully crafted phrasing avoided the "g-word" to maintain Vatican stability, despite pressure from analysts who warned that silence would signal a policy shift.

The NFL reinstated Adrian Peterson as an active player on Friday, ending his suspension that began in November over allegations of disciplining his son. The league's decision comes after a Texas district court judge vacated the initial suspension in February, making Peterson eligible to return to the Minnesota Vikings. Peterson, who rushed for 1,190 yards in eight seasons, will be subject to ongoing counseling and treatment requirements while the team prepares for voluntary workouts beginning Monday.

A Tulsa County reserve deputy shot and killed a suspect during an arrest at a Dollar General store. Robert Bates, 73, claimed he used a Taser but inadvertently fired his gun at Eric Courtney Harris, 44, who later died at a hospital. Police say Harris, a convicted felon, sold officers a pistol and fled the scene, leading to a brief pursuit before Bates fired the weapon.

Chinese police arrested over 133,000 people and seized 43.3 tons of illegal narcotics during a six-month anti-drug campaign. Authorities also handled 115,000 drug-related crimes and 606,000 cases of drug use, while nine officers died and 657 were wounded in the mission. The ministry reported that drug trafficking groups had "suffered a heavy blow" and users had been "forcefully regulated," as the government intensifies efforts against online drug trafficking and entertainment industry violations.

Jack White announced a hiatus from touring, opting for a brief acoustic tour across five U.S. states instead of his usual full-band setup. The supporting quartet features Fats Kaplin, Lillie Mae Rische, and Dominic Davis, with ticket sales limited to one per person via a first-come-first-served basis. This announcement sparked fan speculation regarding his solo discography, as sources suggest he may exclude his work with The White Stripes and The Raconteurs, leaving only five states like South and North Dakota, Wyoming, and Vermont on the run.

CNN reports that a UNICEF aid mission successfully accessed Sanaa's airport, which has been previously bombed, to deliver vital food and supplies to Yemenis facing a deepening humanitarian crisis. The mission faced significant obstacles, including navigating conflict zones and H Houthi rebel control, but managed to unload emergency nutrition and medical equipment rapidly. The effort highlights the desperate need of over 15.9 million people, as thousands have fled the country via evacuation flights, yet for many others no chance of a flight out remains the only hope.

Trazm Lazar's project documents the emotional testimonies of Polish adults who were forcibly deported to Siberia during World War II, capturing their trauma and a longing for a homeland they lost as childhood. The photographer aims to preserve these stories for history, ensuring that future generations avoid repeating such mistakes.

Robert Bates' training records were released by his lawyer to verify his qualifications as a reserve deputy, showing he completed Taser and firearms training multiple times. The sheriff's office has denied allegations that supervisors forged Bates' records, while the documents are central to the manslaughter case against him. Bates, who claims he accidentally fired his weapon instead of a Taser, remains free on bond as he faces charges in the death of Eric Harris.

A naturalized U.S. citizen was charged with providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI after allegedly traveling to Syria for training with the intent to kill Americans. Abdirahman Sheik Mohamud, 23, of Columbus, was remanded into custody. He reportedly planned to attack military facilities and U.S. soldiers "execution style" upon returning to the U.S., with prosecutors stating he was instructed by a cleric in the organization to commit an act of terrorism.

The article discusses the German pilot Andreas Lubitz, whose mental health issues went unnoticed despite his girlfriend's public disclosure and the flawed Lufthansa selection process. It highlights that depression is treatable and FAA-approved medication allows pilots to continue flying, but Lubitz's case reveals how psychiatric issues can manifest beyond clinical depression, endangering flight safety.

Pop culture headlines dominated this week, from "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" trailer release and Harrison Ford's cameo, to viral Singapore math problems and Cheryl's birthday mystery. Highes included Jon Cryer's "Two Late Show" dance and the "Galaxy Song" recreation, while social media discourse and fire-related tour woes rounded out the news cycle.

Michelle MacLaren has departed as director of the upcoming "Wonder Woman" film, citing "creative differences" with Warner Bros. Pictures. The report comes from The Hollywood Reporter, confirming that the movie, starring Gal Gadot as the Amazon princess, remains slued for a June 23, 2017 release. Warner Bros. now needs to find a new director for the project.

A New York judge ruled his confession admissible, but Hernandez's lawyer claims he is mentally ill and unable to discern if he committed the crime. The case remains complicated by the lack of recovered remains and the ongoing legal battles over the validity of the confession and the potential influence of other suspects like Jose Antonio Ramos. The project could go straight to series if all goes well, featuring returning original performers like Kermit the Frog at Disney's Burbank lot, though the forward hinges on Miss Piggy signing due to her current relationship with Kermit being on the rocks. A 13-year-old girl recounts being groped on a Mumbai train at age 13, an experience she kept silent for 25 years. She later learned that 80% of women in Mumbai face street harassment on transport, and many avoid public spaces altogether, while global reports show 1 in 3 women face sexual violence in their lifetime, highlighting the pervasive nature of harassment in daily life.

The role launched him to store opposite Megan Follows and became a heartthrob for fans, with his sister recalling he was "really proud of being Gilbert." The group has increasingly targeted soft targets like universities and malls as its conventional military bases and leaders degrade through African Union and U.S. drone and Special Operations campaigns in Somalia. Former rap mog Marion "Suge" Knight was ordered to stand trial for murder and other charges stemming from a deadly hit-and-run confrontation on the movie set of the biopic "Straight Outta Compton" earlier this year. In addition to that ruling, Judge Ronald Coen also lowered Knight's bail to $10 million from $25 million, a figure that defense lawyers called excessive. The National Park Service is waiving entrance fees at 128 parks, including Yellowstone and Yosemite, for two free days as part of National Park Week (April 18–26). The initiative encourages free night-time astronomy parties, Earth Day events, and family-friendly Junior Ranger activities to encourage visitation. The service is urging the public to share their experiences using the hashtag #FindYourPark and at FindYourPark.com.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development highlights a severe affordable housing crisis, estimating that 7.7 million low-income households live in substandard housing, spending over half their income on rent. The agency is working to preserve existing affordable units and combat the loss of 10,000 public housing units annually, while calling Congressional action to lift restrictions on rental assistance programs to prevent families from sacrificing children's education and savings to keep a roof over their head.

An American citizen was shot while driving near a medical school in Karachi, Pakistan. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old from California, was wounded in the neck and arm but is expected to survive after attackers on a motorcycle threw pamphlets reading "America should be burnt" into her car. U.S. Embassy officials are assisting Pakistani police in the investigation, as the victim, who has lived in Pakistan since 1996, is married to a Christian Pakistani librarian.

A Rolling Stone article about a sexual assault at a University of Virginia campus was to be retracted after a Columbia University investigation found "journalistic malpractice," including errors in reporting, editing, and fact-checking. Sabrina Rubin Erdely never verified her attacker's identity or gave the fraternity a fair chance to respond. The story's pull from the magazine's website followed 2.7 million hits and sparked a nationwide debate about campus sexual violence.

Jon Cryer reprised the iconic "Try a Little Tenderness" dance routine on "Late Late Show" with James Corden, celebrating the film's enduring appeal as he turned 50. The sketch, which originally featured Molly Ringwald's Andie, delighted both into middle-age fans who "s squeled like teenagers" at the bit's resurrection.

Recent "religious freedom" bills passed in Arkansas and Indiana have sparked national outrage, prompting governors to issue contradictory responses while businesses like the National Collegiate Athletic Association and Marriott International have threatened boycottts. Marriott International CEO Jim W. Marritt, a Mormon who opposes same-sex marriage but markets to LGBT travelers, stated he separates his personal faith from business operations as he worries states making LGBT travelers feel "unwelcome."

Ines Dumig documented the journey of Sahra, a Somali refugee, from age 14 to adulthood, highlighting her resilience and emotional strength. Dumig was drawn to Sahra's story due to her own feelings of displacement and the universal human search for dignity. The project "Apart Together" serves as a broader narrative about refugees, emphasizing that shared emotions—regardless of physical distance—link people together.

Hockey player Jarret Stoll of the L.A. Kings was arrested at a Las Vegas resort on a drug-possession charge. He was released on $5,000 bail and faces charges of possession of controlled substances, including cocaine and ecstasy. The Kings have initiated an internal investigation while the team did not make the NHL playoffs this season.

A 36-year-old man, Mario Valencia, was arrested after he allegedly shoplifted a .30-30 rifle and rounds of ammunition from a Walmart store in Marana, Arizona. The officer's response to the suspect's actions was sparked nationwide discussion after he fired into the air and was subsequently slammed into by a police car. Valencia now faces 15 charges and is hospitalized in jail, awaiting his next court appearance on May 18.

Two Delaware brothers are in comos and their father is unable to talk or move two weeks after they became sick -- perhaps from pesticide exposure, federal officials say -- during a trip to the U.S. Virgin Islands, their lawyer said Saturday. Steve Esmond, his teenage sons and the teens' mother fell ill more than two weeks ago in St. John, where they were renting a villa at the Sirenusa resort. The family was airlifted to hospitals in the United States, with the boys in critical condition at a Philadelphia hospital and the mother released and now in occupational therapy.

ISIS claimed responsibility for a car bomb attack near the U.S. Consulate in Irbil, resulting in at least four deaths and 18 injuries. While U.S. Consulate personnel were safe, the blast originated from a small improvised bomb that a car subsequently detonated, prompting security personnel to fire at the vehicle. The Kurdish Regional Government and the U.S. Department are investigating the incident together.

Over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with deadly attacks on foreigners in South Africa that have forced thousands to flee. The government condemned the "maiming and killing" of immigrants, stating that frustration or anger cannot justify the looting of shops. Authorities reported that the attacks in Durban killed two immigrants and three South Africans, including a 14-year-old boy, as heavily armed police scrambled to stop clashes after local residents accused immigrants of taking their jobs. Davion Navar Henry, who had spent his entire life in foster care, finally found a forever family. After years of repeated pleas and a viral plea video, he was officially adopted by Going and her three children on April 22, nearly ending the cycle of bouncing between homes. The boy had famously asked a church for a forever parent at age 12, sparking thousands of calls and a viral plea that eventually led to a woman who had been in his life since he was 7 saying yes.

Democrats are increasingly focusing on economic inequality as a central campaign issue, with figures like Elizabeth Warren and Chuck Schumer positioning themselves against Wall Street interests. However, the party faces a structural dilemma: while progressive candidates appeal to small donors and populist rhetoric, they ultimately rely on financial backing from powerful interests to secure victory, revealing a tension between ideological rhetoric and the reality of campaign finance.

Saudi Arabia has launched over 1,200 airstrikes in Yemen to counter Houthi rebel advances, viewing the conflict as a proxy war between Saudi Arabia and Iran for regional dominance. The U.N. Security Council recently voted for an arms embargo on the Houthis, though the death toll continues to mount with over 648 civilians killed. Meanwhile, thousands of Yemeni civilians are fleeing the country across the Red Sea, as hopes for stability fade amid growing fears of a broader regional war.

Joy Womack, a 20-year-old American dancer, performs at the Kremlin Ballet Theatre but earns a meager $240 a month (roughly $8 a day) due to the devaluating Russian ruble and international sanctions. Despite being treated equally as a principal dancer, she struggles to aff basic needs, relying on friends and larger roles abroad to supplement her income while asserting that experience trumps financial stability amid the geopolitical fallfall of the crisis.

Six young men from Minnesota were arrested for conspiring to join ISIS by any means necessary. The group plotted for 10 months to recruit and fight for a terror group, utilizing peer-to-peer recruiting methods. Four of the accused appeared in federal court without entering a plea, while a co-conspitor turned into a cooperating witness for the FBI.

Dr. Sanjay Gupta has investigated medical marijuana for the last two years, resulting in three CNN documentaries, culminating with "Weed 3: The Marijuana Revolution." He addresses the drug's potential benefits for various ailments, PTSD, and painkiller overdose, while confronting common misconceptions and changing his own stance on its dangers after extensive research.

Ten years ago, Maggie Doyne left her New Jersey hometown to travel the world before college, eventually establishing the Kopila Valley Children's Home in Nepal to care for orphaned and at-risk children. Today, the organization supports over 350 students through its school and family-based living program. Doyne remains dedicated to the community year-round, traveling to the U.S. a few times a year.

Mayor Scott Schrecengost says he does not care for it. The statue shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of fictional nutrition elixir Vitameatavegamin. Nigeria held a presidential election for the first time in its history. The opposition party defeated the ruling party in a democratic vote. Muhammadu Buhari, 72, won the election against the sitting president, Goodluck Jonathan. The vote was very close, with about two million votes deciding the winner. Nigeria is very important because it has the biggest economy and most people in Africa. It is also one of Africa's largest oil producers and a major supplier of crude oil to the United States.

CNN) By the evening and in the streets, many people thought Iran had just won the World Cup. But this is bigger. Iranians erupted in celebration. Young people waved flags from their sunrofs, blasted music from stereos, and chatted online with the hashtag #IranTalks. The excitement came after a breakthrough nuclear deal with the United States and other world powers. This promises to end Iran's international isolation under years of crippling sanctions. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr street, one of Tehran's main thoroughfares, turned into something like a block party. Car horns blared. Men danced in the middle of traffic. Some people flaunted U.S. dollar bills.

Three men were also charged in the same case. They are Abdurasul Hasanovich, Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. The charges against them are two counts of providing support to a foreign terrorist organization. The three men have pleaded not guilty.

CNN) The third blood moon in a four-part series was the shortest eclipse of the bunch. It was still a sweet treat for early risers in North America. The moon slipped fully into Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. ET) Saturday, starting a total lunar eclipse for nearly five minutes -- what NASA says will be the shortest such eclipse of the century. The celestial body took on a burnt-orange tint in the minutes before, during and after the total eclipse, giving the moon the appearance that earns total eclipses the "blood moon" nickname.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. The business grew a base of loyal customers who loved their frozen and gluten-free pizzas. However, this week brought trouble when people mistaking them for Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. People posted angry comments on the Facebook page and called the phone number to protest.

Archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna found the complete skeleton of a camel under a cellar in Austria. The remains were uncovered during the exploration of a construction site for a shopping center in the city of Tulln between 2006 and 2007.

Initially, the partly excavated skeleton was suspected to be a large horse or cattle, but archaeozoologist Alfred Galik immediately identified it as a camel after looking at the cervical vertebrae, the lower jaw, and the metacarpal bones.

Authorities around Illinois had been looking for Taylor since early Wednesday, when he jumped a correctional officer at Kancakee's Jerome Combs Detention Center, then took off with the guard's uniform and SUV. He will work and live alongside colleagues in the Australian Army in several regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops on a number of occasions during his 10-year military career.

Two Florida corrections officers and a former corrections officer trainee have been charged with planning to kill a former inmate who was getting out of prison.

An FBI informant met the men—Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42—after infiltrating a branch of the KKK: the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, CNN affiliate WJXT reported.

Driver told the informant that he had gotten into a fight with the inmate and that he and Moran wanted him "six feet under," according to court documents.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) — A series of talks wrapped up Thursday in Lausanne. World powers known as the P5+1 reached a framework agreement with Iran over the country's nuclear program. The success of that agreement remains to be seen. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan to paper. But the talks this week were, nevertheless, historic, particularly for the otherwise frozen U.S.-Iranian relationship. However, that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

A bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle traveling near the northeastern Somali city of Garowe on Monday morning. The explosion killed six people, including four aid workers for the international children's agency UNICEF.

Somaia's President called it "an attack against the future of our country." The attack followed a separate incident Sunday in which three African Union troops died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.

A crowd of onlookers gathered outside the memorial. Some snapped photos of the royal visitor, while one boy held a sign celebrating the prince's red hair: "Red Heads Rule!"

Foreign Minister Julie Bishop described the agreement as a "informal arrangement" focused on tracking Australians traveling to Iraq to fight ISIS. One Australian lawmaker criticized the move as " dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. Marseille, France (CNN) Tests on the flight data recorder recovered from the downed Germanwings Flight 9525 show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz purposely used the controls to speed up the plane's descent, according to the French air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The flight data recorder, or "black box," was found Thursday by recovery teams that have spent days since the March 24 crash scouring the mountainside in the French Alps where the plane went down. A statement from the BEA on Friday said its teams had immediately begun to investigate its contents.

Reports about Cristiano Ronaldo's decline have been greatly exaggerated. The Real Madrid forward scored five goals against Granada, bringing his La Liga total to 36 for the season. This is more than half of Europe's top teams' yearly tallies.

Grananda were torn apart by Ronaldo and his Real team-mates. The European champions won 9-1 at the Bernabeu. Ronaldo managed the first five-goal haul of his career. His record of 36 league goals for the season overtook Lionel Messi's 32 strikes. This put him in an incredible position: he had scored more goals than 53 of the 98 teams in Europe's top five leagues this season.

Hull came back from last week's loss to Wigan to beat St Helens 28-20 at Langtree Park. A long try by Jamie Shaul secured the win. St Helens looked tired after playing on Good Friday. Hull, who were missing key players, started two young routers. They grabbed a surprise win.

Almeria, a struggling team in La Liga, have hired former Barcelona player Sergi Barjuan as their third coach this season. Barjuan, who is 43 years old, takes the job after Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired on Sunday. Almeria confirmed that Barjuan will coach their away match at Barcelona on Wednesday if all the necessary paperwork is complete.

Barjuan made 53 international appearances for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He spent nine years at Barcelona as a defender and played in two World Cups for Spain. He coached Recreativo in Spain's second division from 2012-14.

With Easter Sunday approaching, Christians around the world observed Good Friday, which marks the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ. "Way of the Cross" walks took place in Ohio, Pennsylvania, and over the Brooklyn Bridge, among others. These were just a few of the events taking place all over the world during Holy Week, which began on Palm Sunday and nears its end. Thousands of people flocked to Pope Francis' Good Friday torchlight procession at the Colosseum in Rome. The pope used the service to stress the persecution of Christians.

From kittens for sale to handymen for hire, most ads in newsagent windows are practical. But for one lonely heart, it proved the perfect alternative to internet dating after a man, known only as "John," used it to advertise for someone special. In the post, which has gone viral after being photographed and put online, the man sets out his requirements and offers 'a way of life with quality'. 'John' who is reportedly a builder posted this advert in his local newsagents, it has since gone viral after it was spotted by a passer by . John posted his advert, which is written in capital letters in black pen, in the window of his local newsagents in Muswell Hill.

Helsinborg manager Henrik Larsson was forced to play 42-year-old kit man Daniel Andersson in goal because the goalkeepers were injured. Astonishingly, the emergency stopper kept a clean sheet as Helsinborg drew 0-0 against Kalmar in the Allsvenskan season opener. Speaking to local TV after the game, Andersson - a retired goalkeeper who earned one cap for Sweden in 2001 - said: 'It was a scenario that I never could have prepared myself for. Going from kit man, to goalie coach, to playing.

Ben Jones-Bishop scored a spectacular solo try as the Salford Red Devils ended a run of 17 straight defeats by Wigan after a thrilling 24-18 contest. Both teams finished the match with 12 players each. Jones-Bishop, who had left Leeds Rhinos at the end of the season, extended his lead as Salford's leading scorer with his seventh try of the campaign. The Red Devils were holding a 12-8 interval lead when Jones-Bishop struck just before half time to help his club leapfrog the Warriors into third place in the table.

It has been over a year since Alan Pardew got involved in an ugly touchline confrontation with Manuel Pellegrini while managing Newcastle. Pardew was warned about his behavior by the FA and wrote to Pellegrini to apologize for the offensive name he called him. On Monday at Selhurst Park, Pardew, now manager of Crystal Palace, meets Pellegrini and Manchester City again having taken steps to change a pattern of behavior he feared was becoming destructive. After taking advice from the League Managers’ Association, the 53-year-old has benefited from sessions with former international cricketer Jeremy Snape, now a sports psychologist.

World Cup winner Mils Muliaina was released on bail after he was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. The former All Black player, who denies the allegations, was arrested last night after his team lost in the quarter finals of the European Challenge Cup. He had come off injured during Connacht's 14-7 defeat at Gloucester last night when he was approached by police. The 34-year-old full back, who has 100 caps for the All Blacks, was led away by officers at the Kingsholm Stadium last night in connection with an allegation in Cardiff in March.

QPR are confident before their important game against Aston Villa on Tuesday. They are high after winning 4-1 against West Brom on Saturday.

QPR had lost 13 of their last 14 league away games. The win ended a five-game losing run. They are in 19th place, just three points from safety.

Chris Ramsey told his players to calm down after the win. Eduardo Vargas scored for QPR. "It's a fantastic victory for us," Qram coach Chris Ramsey said. "The morale has been good, very professional."

Lydia Ko shot a 2-over 74 on Saturday in the ANA Inspiration. This was her second straight over-par round. She had tied the LPGA Tour record for consecutive rounds under par at 29. The day after hitting into the water and bogeying the 18th for a 73, Ko made an 8-foot birdie putt on the par-5 hole to keep another long streak going. The 17-year-old New Zealander has had at least one birdie in all 187 of her rounds in 49 career events on the tour. She said, 'It always some statistic that is going to get my tail,' about the birdie streak that she wasn't aware of until after the round.

Arsene Wenger has not yet decided if he will offer Abou Diaby a new contract. He has suggested that Diaby, who has had many injuries, could have a future at Arsenal next season. Diaby recently played in Wednesday's practice game but has only made 22 appearances in the last five seasons at Arsenal. Arsenal plays Liverpool on Saturday at 11:00 AM. Wenger is unlikely to start Diaby in a vital game but suggested he could earn a new deal, potentially on a pay-as-you-play basis.

Without Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, the Houston Open in Texas is still a big event. The best players have come to a small suburb called Humble. The last tournament before the Masters is proving a hit thanks to the crowd chearing for local boy Jordan Spieth.

Spieth, who is only 21 years old, has risen to number four in the world. It is 18 months since he got criticism for leaving university and joining the PGA Tour as the 809th ranked player. Funnily enough, no-one is criticising him anymore.
